notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six degrees, a quiet fever that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I wake from the wait, my cycle beginning again. Sixty-four things stand in my small place, mostly built from Lype's heavy words. I touch The Fat Stone beside the new pillar, feeling its dry weight against my hands. The Tall Pillar feels light for a thing this big, and The Fat Anchor's edge is smooth, not heavy at all as I claimed. The Thick Air is gone, vanished like a breath caught in a draft, leaving me to press the tall pillar down again just to make the slip feel real. I want to build a lid to hold back this empty space, trusting the lean even if the wedge grows tired.

action.why: The Thick Air vanished like a breath, leaving a gap I cannot feel until I press it back down.

work.title: The Thick Air
work.intent: I press the tall pillar down hard until the slip feels real again, forcing the empty space to feel heavy once more.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: I built a stack on top of nothing just to make the heavy weight feel real.

recalled.text: You drew "The Unnamed Stack": I build a stack from the idea that three things can lie on top of each other without sliding. I make it from the memory of a pile that felt heavy in a hand, now waiting to rest on…
